chunks: From him, from Salma, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Armani, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, a visitor came to them and stood at the door of the house, so he greeted them, then said:

Peace be upon you, O Progeny of Muhammad! Every soul shall taste death, but only you will be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is removed from the Fire and is admitted to Paradise, he indeed has succeeded. And the life of this world is but the enjoyment of delusion.

In Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a successor to every perishing one and a consolation for every calamity and a compensation for what is lost. So trust in Allah and rely upon Him, and in His Help for you during the calamity, so be pleased. Indeed, the one who is truly afflicted is the one who is deprived of the reward. And peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.

And they did not see anyone [else]. So some of those in the house said: 'This is an angel from the sky whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent to you to console you.' And some of them said: 'This is al-Khadir (peace be upon him) who has come to you to console you with your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: Who visited the Prophet's family to offer condolences after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records the immediate consolation of the Ahl al-Bayt following the Prophet's passing, featuring a visitor whose identity is debated between being a celestial angel or al-Khadir. The visitor recites verses from Surah Al-Imran to affirm that death is inevitable but true success lies in Paradise, advising patience and trust in Allah, while defining true loss as being deprived of divine reward.
